problem_context.statement: Given two strings s and t, return true if t can be formed by rearranging exactly the characters of s; otherwise return false.

examples.explanation: Both strings have the same character counts.

problem_context.title: Valid Anagram
constraints: s and t contain lowercase English letters.

expected_approaches.summary: Reject unequal lengths, increment counts for one string, then decrement for the other.
expected_approaches.applicability: Strings whose character identity can be counted.
assumptions: The chosen count representation covers the input character domain.
key_invariants: After processing prefixes of equal length, each count is the remaining excess from s over t.
expected_approaches.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed 26-letter candidate contract; O(k) for a generalized character domain of size k
tradeoffs: A fixed alphabet can use an array; broader text needs a map.

alternative_approaches.summary: Sort both character sequences and compare their ordered forms.
key_invariants: Equal multisets have identical sorted sequences.
tradeoffs: Simpler to explain but slower than frequency counting.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: bool isAnagram(string s,string t){ if(s.size()!=t.size()) return false; int count[26]={}; for(char c:s) ++count[c-'a']; for(char c:t) if(--count[c-'a']<0) return false; return true; } };

class Solution { public boolean isAnagram(String s,String t){ if(s.length()!=t.length()) return false; int[] count=new int[26]; for(char c:s.toCharArray()) count[c-'a']++; for(char c:t.toCharArray()) if(--count[c-'a']<0) return false; return true; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: Each count represents unmatched occurrences after equal processing progress.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Distinguish linear scans from sorting's logarithmic factor and explain why the 26-slot count array is O(1) under the lowercase-English contract.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Require equal multiplicities, not merely the same distinct characters.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Reject different lengths before accepting matching partial counts.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Two empty strings have equal character multisets.

counterexamples.purpose: The strings share characters but have different counts.
An anagram must have equal total length.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Choose a map or another representation if fixed lowercase indexing is invalid.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why a negative decrement proves a missing character occurrence.
Test whether the candidate recognizes the character-domain assumption.

expected_good_signals: tracks counts rather than membership alone
sample_phrasings: What would distinguish these strings when their character sets match?

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Clarify the input-domain assumption behind fixed indexing.
expected_good_signals: chooses a map for broader characters
sample_phrasings: What would change if the input were not limited to lowercase letters?

expected_good_signals: identifies sorting's O(n log n) cost
weak_or_misconception_signals: calls both approaches equivalent in cost
sample_phrasings: What tradeoff are you making by sorting the strings?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on count correctness and duplicate characters.
Expect the alphabet-domain assumption to be explicit.

pack.reference_reasoning: Frequency counting is the reviewed primary prior, but a candidate may present other correct ways to compare character multisets.

input.candidate_statement: I compare the counts, but I have not described the representation.

technical_rationale_rubric.technical_issue: Clarify which representation is used without treating prior context as proof of a present error.
